STEP 1 — goal: read the specification against the idea and list candidate defects.
Read: (there is no workspace file; the idea, idea equations, idea coupling/ablations and the full specification are in the task text).
Observations (candidate defects):
(1) computations.quantised_value: definition "x_q = P + (one_hot(k_l(i)) - P).detach()" has forward value one_hot(k_l(i)), i.e. shape B x K = B x 256, while the output field claims "x_q (B x d)" with d = 32 and the note claims "the forward value is exactly the chosen RAW codeword E_{k_l(i)}". Both cannot hold: no codebook multiply appears in the algebraic part. The backward is the identity on P only for the one-hot form; a codeword-valued form x_q = P@E + (E_k - P@E).detach() has backward E^T into P. The idea itself asserted the same wrong sentence, but the spec is supposed to be mathematically correct, so this must be repaired.
(2) mechanism paragraph: "...the reconstruction's gradient reaches the cost, and through it v_i, u_k and the behaviour field's parameters." This contradicts the spec's own gradient rule ("the behaviour field ... no gradient") and the idea ("t_i and n_i are detached per-epoch constants; gradients flow only through v_i and u_k"). gradient_rules entry 2 also says "C depends on ... the behaviour field through Delta_i", which must read "as a detached constant".
(3) conventions.distance: the idea gives d_P = (1/sqrt(c)) artanh(...); the spec uses (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(...) and calls the idea's form "informal ... CORRECTED". It is not informality: the factor 2 doubles C with the baseline's fixed epsilon, halves the effective entropic temperature and therefore changes the plan and the assignment (the spec's own sentence says exactly this). This is a change of the idea, requiring an explicit amendment of the idea record (or the factor-1 implementation with the matching lambda and displacement exp_0(m_i n_i) instead of exp_0((m_i/2) n_i)).
(4) computations.distance.domain: interiority is justified by "both the item point and the code point are the LIFTED images"; q_{i,k} = u_k (+) Delta_i is a Möbius sum, not a lift. Correct justification: closure of Möbius addition in the ball.
(5) computations.sinkhorn_plan.note: "the baseline's own level-3 rule centres its distances first; the mechanism does not ... so the plan's temperature is the cost's own scale". In entropic OT with fixed marginals the plan is invariant to additive row/column shifts of C (they are absorbed by the scaling vectors), so omitting the centring changes nothing and cannot change the temperature; the only scale change is the x2 of finding (3).
Still open: whether the ball/displacement identities and the switches are internally consistent (checked next).

STEP 2 — goal: verify the geometry, the limits and the switches before fixing the verdict.
Read: conventions (distance, exponential_map, logarithm, tangent_norm, lift, plan), computations ball_lift / code_lift / displacement / displaced_code / distance / nearest_code_distance / arc_length, continuous_surface statements + executable, switch_behaviour, switch_geometry.
Observations (all correct, no finding): exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)v/(sqrt(c)||v||) = tanhc(sqrt(c)||v||)v matches ball_lift and the idea's (1/sqrt(c))tanh(sqrt(c)||r||/q) r/||r||; log_x^c(y) = (2/(sqrt(c) lambda_x)) artanh(min(...)) w/max(||w||,1e-12) is the coordinate log consistent with the factor-2 metric (||log||_coord = d/lambda_x); the clip 1-1e-5 and the artanh(0)=0 limit are consistent with the distance; with the factor-2 metric d_c(0, exp_0^c(v)) = 2||v|| so Delta_i = exp_0^c((m_i/2)n_i) gives d_c(0,Delta_i) = m_i and (left invariance) d_c(u_k, q_{i,k}) = m_i; M_i, n_i as coordinate pair matches the idea's ||t_i|| and t_i/||t_i||; d_nn_i detached equals the BEHAV=off row minimum; m_i = min(M_i, 0.5 d_nn_i) matches the idea; Möbius formula in displaced_code and in continuous_surface.statements is the standard one and the executable matches it (only an additive 1e-12 in the denominator, harmless); the c->0 branch 2||x-(u+p)|| is the stated limit; the lift is bounded (tanh<1, ball radius 1/sqrt(c)=1) and Mobius sums stay inside, so the clip is never reached in exact arithmetic. Switches: BEHAV=off gives Delta=0, q=u, C=d_c(v_i,u_k) exactly as the idea's ablation; GEOM=euclid keeps the c=1 field and switches only the metric, as the idea states.
Conclusion so far: the geometry, the limits, the sign of the cap and both switches are faithful; the defects are the five textual/mathematical ones from STEP 1 (quantised_value forward value and shape, gradient into the behaviour field, the x2 metric scale change, the wrong domain justification, the wrong centring/temperature claim).
Still open: nothing else; writing the tests and the verdict next.

Step 1: Goal — review the provided mathematical specification against the IDEA. Read the task text (idea, idea spec, idea equations, specification JSON) from the prompt; no workspace files provided/needed. Initial observation: the spec claims to use the framework's factor-2 Poincare distance (2/sqrt(c) artanh) while the IDEA states d_P = (1/sqrt(c)) artanh(...). The spec declares this as a "recorded correction". I need to check whether (a) the factor-2 change is faithful/justified, (b) the displacement identity is dimensionally and mathematically consistent, (c) the lift formula matches between the idea and the spec, (d) the BEHAV/GEOM switches do what they claim, (e) the gradient path is stated. Open: verify algebra of the displacement claim d_c(0,Delta)=m_i and whether "arc length" language is consistent with the tanh (not tanhc) form used in displaced_code vs displacement.

Step 2: Checks performed (all arithmetic done by hand on the spec's own strings).
(1) LIFT: spec v=tanhc(sqrt(c)||r/q||)(r/q) with tanhc(a)=tanh(a)/a equals idea's (1/sqrt c)tanh(sqrt(c)||r||/q) r/||r|| — OK, faithful.
(2) DISPLACEMENT: Delta=exp_0((m/2)n)=(1/sqrt c)tanh(sqrt c m/2)n equals idea's tanh(sqrt c m/2)/sqrt(c) n — OK; and with d_c=(2/sqrt c)artanh, d_c(0,Delta)=(2/sqrt c)(sqrt c m/2)=m, so the "origin distance exactly m_i" claim holds and the /2 is consistent ONLY with the factor-2 metric. The factor-2 vs the informal (1/sqrt c) of the idea text is resolved by the idea's own equations (l3: "framework's factor 2, c->0 limit 2||x-y||"), so I do NOT file it.
(3) MOBIUS formula, continuous_surface statements and executable, c->0 limit (lift->v, mobius->x+y, d0=2||x-y||) all verified correct. Surface statements match the mobius closed form.
(4) DEFECT A found: computations.successor_snapshot says "for l = 3 ... r_{s,3} = z_s - E_{k_2(s)}" — drops the level-1 row; level_residual defines r=z-sum_{j<l}E_{k_j}, so r_{s,3}=z_s-E_{k_1(s)}-E_{k_2(s)}. V_3 would be the lift of a residual the mechanism never uses.
(5) DEFECT B found: sinkhorn_plan note + conventions.plan: the baseline's level-3 rule rescales its distances to [-1,1] before Sinkhorn, while the mechanism feeds C "unchanged"/"no centring" and admits a different temperature. That changes the plan operator (entropic weight vs cost scale), contradicting idea's "the baseline's Sinkhorn (same epsilon ... same plan extraction)" and making the BEHAV=off arm not the baseline plan.
(6) DEFECT C found: gradient path. gradient_rules/conventions define "residual = (residual - quant).detach()" (value chain), which makes r_{i,l} (l>=2) a stop-gradient constant, hence v_i = lift(r/q) a constant with no gradient to z; but mechanism and the cost gradient rule assert the reconstruction's gradient reaches "the item point v_i" and that level_residual/level_residual output is "differentiable: true". Either r must be z_i - sum sg(E_{k_j}) (z attached) or the claims must be withdrawn.
(7) DEFECT D found: mechanism says the reconstruction's gradient reaches "the displacement's parameters", but the field (t,n,M,m,Delta) is detached and parameters lists no such parameters — no such gradient path exists.
Still open: nothing; verdict REVISE with 4 findings, each with a spec-only check(spec).

Final answer (review of the specification against the idea). Verdict REVISE, four findings, each with a spec-only check(spec).
